Agenda

  1. Review previous sprint outcomes and carry-over work (10 min)
  2. Confirm sprint goal (10 min)
  3. Review and prioritise the backlog candidates (25 min)
  4. Capacity check and commitment (10 min)
  5. Risks, dependencies and open questions (5 min)

Discussion

1. Review of Sprint 23 outcomes and carry-over

Sprint 23 closed with 14 of 17 committed story points delivered (82%). Two stories carried over: the email verification retry flow (blocked on a vendor API key until Thursday) and the analytics event schema update (QA found a regression late in the sprint). Lee noted that both regressions were caught before release. Daniel flagged that the vendor key delay was the main cause of slippage and asked that secrets requests be raised at sprint start, not mid-sprint.

2. Sprint goal

Maya proposed the goal: ship self-serve onboarding v1 to 100% of new signups. Aisha said the goal is clear but should explicitly exclude the enterprise invite flow, which is a separate track. The group agreed and added that success will be measured by onboarding completion rate, tracked from the first day of rollout.

3. Backlog review and prioritisation

Eleven candidate items were reviewed. Discussion centred on three:

  • Onboarding checklist UI — Priya confirmed the component is ready; the remaining work is responsive layout on small screens. Must-have.
  • Progress-saving across sessions — Tomás noted this requires a schema migration on the user profile table. Estimated at 5 points; the team wants it scheduled early so the migration can be verified in staging. Must-have.
  • Skip-for-now analytics tagging — Grace (via async input) asked that events fire from day one. Nice-to-have if capacity allows, but instrumentation for the core flow is non-negotiable.

The enterprise invite flow and the dark-mode settings page were deferred to the backlog for future refinement.

4. Capacity and commitment

Team capacity is 42 points across six engineers after accounting for the planned on-call rotation and the public holiday on Thursday, November 26. The team committed to 34 points, leaving a buffer of 8 points for unplanned work and bugs. Lee asked for at least one day of QA time to be reserved in the final three days of the sprint for regression testing.

5. Risks and dependencies

  • Vendor API key for the email provider must be confirmed before Day 2 of the sprint.
  • The profile schema migration depends on a staging database refresh; the timing is not yet confirmed.
  • Legal has not yet signed off on the updated consent copy shown during onboarding.

Decisions

D1. Sprint 24 goal: ship self-serve onboarding v1 to 100% of new signups. Enterprise invite flow is out of scope.
D2. Progress-saving and the onboarding checklist UI are must-haves. Analytics tagging for the core flow is must-have; extended analytics is a stretch goal.
D3. Team commits to 34 story points, leaving an 8-point buffer.
D4. Secrets and third-party access requests are raised at sprint kickoff going forward, not mid-sprint.
D5. Enterprise invite flow and dark-mode settings page move to the backlog for refinement in the next session.

Open Questions

  • Can the staging database refresh happen before Wednesday, or does the migration need to move to the second week?
  • What is the exact definition of "onboarding completion" for the success metric (all steps, or required steps only)?
  • Should progress-saving be behind a feature flag so it can be disabled without a rollback?
  • Who is the on-call engineer for the week of Nov 30, and does that reduce the 42-point capacity further?
